messages:
anna: Kicked off a CI sweep that focuses on sequence-length-aware kernel picks + KV cache enabled/disabled permutations. Posting raw notes from the run.

ci-bot: Automated report uploaded to /ci/artifacts/1771234567/seqlen-scan.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
ci-bot: summary: 48 runs, 3 regressions flagged, 2 flaky cases, 43 ok

mike: Nice. Which kernels did we test?

anna: matmul-v1, matmul-v2, fused-attn, flash-attn-quant, and the new tiled-gemm prototype. Tested on A100/H100 (GDS off) and a small intel-gpu node for sanity.

sasha: Sequence lengths: 16, 64, 256, 512, 1024, 2048. Batches: 1, 4, 8. KV caching toggled true/false.

jin: Any dramatic winners?

ci-bot: Top picks by throughput (tokens/s) on H100 (causal, kv=false):
- seq<=64: matmul-v2 (+12% vs baseline)
- seq 256-512: flash-attn-quant (+8% with quant profile q8_5)
- seq>=1024: tiled-gemm prototype (+20% for large matrix paths)

mike: That aligns with expectations. What about kv=true?

ci-bot: With KV cache enabled on H100:
- seq<=64: matmul-v2 still best
- seq 256: flash-attn-quant competitive, but throughput drops ~5%
- seq >=1024: matmul-v2 experienced regression on 2/6 runs (15% slower vs baseline) when kv=true

anna: We tripped a regression: long seq + kv enabled + matmul-v2 on H100. Logs show non-coalesced loads in the attention kernel.

sasha: Reproducer (short):
```
./bench_kernel --model llama-13b --seq 2048 --batch 4 --kernel matmul-v2 --kv-cache on --device h100
```
Observed perf: baseline matmul-v1 = 120 tok/s, matmul-v2 = 102 tok/s (avg), tiled-gemm = 135 tok/s

mike: Hmm. Could be GV100->H100 register tiling assumptions. matmul-v2 expects 128B-aligned KV pages but our cache packing uses 64B strides for >1024 sequences.

jin: I dug into the perf counters: uncoalesced global loads spike when seq>=1024 and kv enabled. Req/warp memory ops up 28%.

anna: Repro case attached in artifacts. Suggest two short fixes: 1) fallback matmul-v1 when kv_enabled && seq>=1024 on H100, 2) quick KV packing alignment patch in runtime.

sasha: For autotune: we should make kernel selector aware of (device_arch, seq_len_bucket, kv_flag, batch_size). Current selector only used device_arch + batch.

mike: Proposal for selector rules (pseudocode):
```
if kv_enabled:
  if seq >= 1024 and device == H100: pick matmul-v1
  elif seq >= 512 and device in [A100, H100]: pick tiled-gemm
  else: pick matmul-v2
else:
  use autotune table baseline
```
We can make this table fed from nightly CI stats.

jin: Also add microbench that exercises misaligned KV strides to catch regressions. Minimal test: seq=1536, kv stride=64 vs kv stride=128.

ci-bot: Added a failing CI test: eng-runtime/seqlen-kv-alignment.test flagged (flake threshold >2 runs).

anna: Action items:
- @mike: add fallback rule to selector and run full CI (small change, should be low risk) :spiral_calendar:
- @jin: open PR with KV packing alignment fix and perf counters in debug build
- @sasha: extend microbench harness with seqlen/kv_stride sweep and add to nightly-scan matrix

mike: Will do. Quick question: how do we push new kernel picks to Dedicated clusters? Need config path.

anna: Picks live in /configs/kernel_picker.json in the control plane. We'll add an override key per deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private). Default rollout = canary 5% -> 20% -> 100%.

sasha: Suggest one more guard: if runtime detects >10% regression vs baseline for 5m, auto-fallback to safe kernel and alert SRE.

jin: Agree. Also let's record token latency p50/p95 in the CI artifacts for future regression detection.

ci-bot: Next scheduled nightly sweep will include sequences up to 4096 for tiled-gemm tests (disabled by default for cost reasons).

mike: I'll iterate on the selector PR today. Reproducer + perf logs in the PR description.

anna: Thanks team. If the selector change is low risk we can patch the canary tonight. I'll coordinate with @oncall for a short maintenance window. :thumbsup:

sasha: One more note — the tiled-gemm prototype has a memory footprint increase at seq>=2048; test added to CI to check peak resident memory and fail if >10% over baseline.

jin: Great. I'll follow up with perf counter dashboards for KV alignment metrics next week.

mike: ETA for PRs: selector PR by EOD, KV packing PR by EOW.

anna: Marking done here for now. Followups in the task board: INF-1223 (selector), INF-1224 (kv packing), INF-1225 (microbench matrix).

sasha: :rocket:

ci-bot: Thread closed (auto) — reopen if new findings are pushed to /ci/artifacts/1771234567/"
